title: opportunistic-span-buffer-and-async-instrumentation-shim
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Background: Mobile and edge clients are sensitive to telemetry overheads. Current SDKs create and emit spans synchronously which increases tail latency and CPU usage for short-lived requests (e.g., inference calls). We need a lightweight, async-safe instrumentation shim that buffers span events opportunistically in a bounded in-memory ring buffer and flushes them out-of-band. The design should preserve essential trace continuity (trace IDs, parent relationships) while being loss-tolerant for non-critical spans and providing deterministic ordering for root-level spans used by latency dashboards.

Goals: implement a cross-language shim (Node/Python/Go) that: 1) adds an in-process bounded span buffer with backpressure-aware flush triggers; 2) exposes a minimal middleware API for HTTP/gRPC/WS to attach/propagate an opaque provenance token in headers; 3) supports sampling hints from the server (sampling_score) and honors priority sampling for high-cost requests; 4) provides a small compatibility shim for existing OpenTelemetry hooks so integration requires minimal changes; 5) emits batched envelope payloads to the telemetry collector over the existing batched ingest endpoint with retry/backoff and jitter.

Constraints: must add <5ms median overhead to fast paths under typical client loads, bounded memory footprint (<1MB by default), avoid blocking application RPC threads, and operate in degraded mode (best-effort) when network or collector is unavailable.

Proposed design: 1) SpanBuffer: lock-free ring buffer per-process with configurable capacity and eviction policy (LRU by age for spans older than X ms). 2) Flush triggers: timer-based (idle flush after 50ms), size-based (batch when buffer >= 50 spans), event-based (on high-priority span or process shutdown), and backpressure-aware (if outgoing channel congested, switch to sampling-only mode). 3) Provenance token: generate an 8-byte opaque token per request, propagated via header X-RW-Provenance (base64url) used to correlate request logs with buffered spans; token->sequence stamps allow best-effort reassembly in collector. 4) Sampling hints: middleware can set sampling_score in response headers (X-RW-Sampling) which SDK honors to promote/demote span emission. 5) Exporter: batched JSONL envelopes with compressed payloads, exponential backoff + capped retries, and optional local filesystem spill-to-disk for critical spans when memory and network are saturated. 6) Compatibility: small adapter layer that maps existing OpenTelemetry Span/Context operations to the buffer API and adds non-blocking instrumentation hooks for async fibers/event loops.

Deliverables: SDK changes (Node/Python/Go), middleware adapters for express/grpc/fastapi, collector-side correlator support in telemetry pipeline, docs and migration guide, test harness and benchmarks.
acceptance_criteria: Node/Python/Go SDKs include the opportunistic span buffer and an opt-out runtime flag
End-to-end test demonstrating header-based provenance token correlates request -> buffered spans in collector test harness
Median overhead of instrumentation <5ms for 95% of client request profiles (benchmark validated)
Buffer capacity defaults to 256 spans, configurable per-deployment; no unbounded memory growth in stress tests
Collector can reassemble and display buffered spans in the existing latency dashboard for promoted traces
Fail-open behavior: SDK does not block application requests when collector is down; drops non-critical spans after configurable retention policy
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag rw.opportunistic_span_buffer=false by default for hosted customers
Alpha rollout to internal telemetry-enabled services and 2 pilot customers for two weeks
Collect performance telemetry and sampling coverage; iterate on defaults (buffer size, flush intervals)
Gradual enable by region and customer tier with monitoring runbooks and quick rollback flag
Ship SDK minor releases with documented migration notes and examples
testing_plan: Unit tests for ring buffer eviction and ordering semantics
Integration test: simulated mobile client with intermittent connectivity, validate spill-to-disk and retry path
Load benchmark against existing sync-emitter: compare p50/p95 latency and CPU allocations for 10k RPS scenario
Chaos test: drop collector connectivity and assert application request latencies do not increase and critical spans eventually arrive or are correctly dropped
Property test for provenance token mapping and de-duplication in collector correlator
monitoring_alerts: Alert if avg flush_latency_ms > 500ms for 10m across production
Alert if dropped_spans / flush_count > 5% sustained for 15m
Alert if emitter retry rate spikes (emit_retries > 100/min) indicating collector problems

2026-03-09 - Priya Nair (Observability): Collector-side correlator will need sequence stamp support; opened collector story ENG-219110 to accept provenance token and sequences.
2026-03-11 - QA: Added test matrix for spill-to-disk behavior. Noted that mobile sandbox denies filesystem writes on some platforms; need fallback to in-memory capped queue only for those platforms.
2026-03-12 - Security review note: briefed security on the opaque token header; token contains no PII and is rotated per-request; security okayed header scheme.
2026-03-14 - Liam Chen: Prototype PR ready for review (Node adapter). Performance harness shows p95 latency reduced relative to sync emitter under bursty workload. Pushing Python/Go adapters next.
